scope: Focused offline comparison of DS1522+ and DS1525+ OEM CPM board initialization, to assess the existing 130-byte DS1522 platform0 topology/clock candidate before expensive V1500B rework. No NAS access, firmware execution or firmware writes by this worker.

conclusion.judgment: The DS1525 reference corroborates the direction of the candidate: V1500B has a board-specific platform0 topology using normal PCIe engines, disabled ASPM, always-enabled clock requests, and native SATA flags matching the candidate. It does not corroborate copying the DS1525 lane/BDF/GPIO layout onto DS1522.
conclusion.recommendation: Keep the current DS1522 board topology/clock candidate unchanged on the strength of this comparison alone. No missing mandatory reset mapping or clock policy was demonstrated. This is corroboration, not hardware validation or GO authorization.
conclusion.remaining_concrete_gap: The candidate's five-port lane combination, especially separate x1 PCIe engines on logical lanes0 and1, has not been observed on V1500B. DS1525 instead uses a combined x2 engine on0..1 and a different board layout. Static comparison alone cannot show successful link training on the DS1522 wiring.

observations.claim: Eleven OEM CPM table bodies match exactly across the two firmwares: $A00,$A01,$A02,$A03,$A11,$A12,$A13,$A14,$A15,$A80,$A81. Differences are concentrated in $A10 GPIO initialization, both $A17 clock tables, and both $A26 DXIO tables.
observations.implication: The comparison is not merely a similarity of product specifications; the class/platform conversion tables and several board policy tables are identical.

observations.kind: Static code byte identity after explicit relocation normalization
observations.claim: AmdCpmInitPeim, AmdCpmGpioInitPeim and AmdCpmPcieInitPeim have identical complete .text bytes after subtracting image base only at PE IMAGE_REL_BASED_HIGHLOW locations. Their .text sizes are14656,4064 and2656 bytes respectively.
observations.implication: Both OEM datasets are interpreted by the same CPM class selector, GPIO/reset consumer and PCIe publisher code. This does not establish that all AGESA/SMU code is identical.

observations.implication: DS1525's production-oriented topology is in platform0 while DS1522's is in platform8. The DS1525 data directly contradicts treating the DS1522 two-PCIe/Ethernet platform0 template as a universal V1500B requirement.
observations.limitation: Selection of platform0 in the historical failed V1500B boot remains an inference, not a captured value.

observations.claim: All active PCIe ports in DS1525 platform0 and the DS1522 candidate have the same non-address policy bits: ASPM0, L1.1=0, L1.2=0, clock-request nibble0xf. Their $A17 clock rows have clock request0xff, slot-check0 and special-function0.
observations.candidate: These DS1522 clock rows are already copied into candidate platform0, preserving the header/platform mask. No further DS1525 clock row is needed to match this policy.

observations.kind: Actual target decompilation plus direct data comparison
observations.claim: The callback requests $A15 and $A06, then searches $A15 for an exact DeviceId and Mode. It executes or queues a reset operation only on a matching record. It does not treat any supplied group ID as a physical GPIO number.
observations.implication: The working DS1525 configuration itself does not add reset-table mappings for IDs35–42. Their absence in the candidate is not a demonstrated omission. Physical reset-net assignments remain outside this table; group IDs must not be relabelled as GPIO numbers.

observations.claim: The GPIO initialization tables have16 pin-keyed differences. These include changed settings for21,22,24,84,85,87,132; removed records30,70,75,88,108; and added records136,138,141,143. The current candidate retains the complete DS1522 GPIO table.
observations.implication: There are concrete pin-policy differences, so the DS1525 GPIO table is not a valid generic V1500B transplant. None was demonstrated to be mandatory for a V1500B installed on the DS1522 board.

observations.kind: New OEM callback difference with a bounded source interpretation
observations.claim: DS1525 adds a scan for GPIO0x57. If its setting has bit11 set and a nonzero IOMUX field, it calls CPM+0x68 on ACPI-MMIO-base+0x354 with AND0x7f and OR0. The common CPM code sets the base to0xfed80000 for classes11/12 and CPM+0x68 is the 8-bit AND/OR helper.
observations.interpretation: Picasso definitions identify PMIO0x54 bit7 as SERIRQ_ENABLE and GPIO87 IOMUX0 as SERIRQ/IOMUX2 as GPIO. This supports interpretation as disabling serial-IRQ signaling when the pin is repurposed. It is not an identified PCIe reset/clock operation.
observations.candidate_implication: A concrete newer callback difference exists, but no evidence establishes it as a mandatory addition to the DS1522 topology candidate.
observations.other_observed_difference_delegated_to_c: PCD0x4f0a0 changes from0xf0b7 to72000; PCD0x4f0a2 from0x6065 to40000. These constants were sent to the main agent for the independent CPU-policy comparison; their meaning is not established by this board-only subtask.

observations.claim: Candidate and DS1525 platform0 both use SATA engines on logical3 and2 with descriptor byte+5=1. The official DTBs retain native SATA at root00:08.2, while the external first-three-bay path differs00:01.5 versus00:01.6.
observations.usb: No USB-engine descriptor occurs in either model's selected $A26 table. This focused CPM table comparison therefore demonstrates no mandatory native-USB change; it is not a complete audit of FCH USB configuration.

observations.claim: Direct comparison reconfirms exactly130 changed bytes, all inside platform0 $A17/$A26 bodies. Candidate clock and DXIO bodies equal original DS1522 platform8 bodies exactly; $A10 GPIO and $A15 reset tables remain identical to original.
